extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for Area Chairs at ICLR 2022 on managing the review process: bidding, vetting reviewers, moderating multi-stage discussion, identifying ethics issues, making accept/reject recommendations, and writing meta-reviews that summarize reviews and discussion. Includes timelines and procedural expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bid on abstracts
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This year we added an abstract submission deadline so ACs should bid on abstracts; having abstracts earlier allows ACs to recommend appropriate reviewers and check reviewer fit early in the reviewing period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vet and recommend reviewer assignments
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assigned a batch of papers, please recommend a set of appropriate reviewers (you may skip this, and the reviewers will be assigned based on their bids only). Ensure reviewer-paper fit and recommend replacements when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify delinquent reviewers and assign alternates
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify delinquent reviewers and assign alternate reviewers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When some reviewers are delinquent or not responsive, help assign alternate reviewers in a timely manner so that every submission gets a chance to be judged fairly and expertly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make final recommendation (accept/reject)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend whether each submission should be accepted or rejected
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For every submission that goes through the reviewing process, recommend accept or reject accompanied by a metareview summarizing the reviews and the three stages of discussion, optionally adding your own view of the paper's merits and limitations. Senior Area Chairs and Program Chairs will engage in decision making; AC recommendations are non-binding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write metareviews summarizing reviews and discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Write metareviews with recommendations for accept/reject
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meta-reviews should summarize the reviews and the three stages of discussion, include your own view if appropriate, and justify your recommendation. Provide clear reasoning based on content and discussion. Aim for thoroughness and clarity so authors understand the decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flag papers for desk reject and escalate ethics concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Flag papers for desk reject; watch out for reviewers' flags for Code of Ethics violations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For all papers flagged, collect information, make an informed recommendation, and provide any evidence obtained (e.g., from the paper, discussion with author and/or reviewers). Note AC recommendation may be passed to the Ethics board for further review and is non-binding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure reviewers follow ICLR reviewer guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure reviewers’ judgments are in line with the new ICLR 2022 reviewer guidelines
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pay special attention to FAQs (e.g., definition of contemporaneous work for citations and empirical comparisons). Ensure reviewer evaluations adhere to the conference's stated review criteria and guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use constructive and polite language
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure the language used in the reviews (including ACs’ own metareviews) are constructive and polite
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a tone of professional, constructive criticism (see suggestion: Daniel Dennett, 'Criticising with Kindness'). Avoid hostile or personal language; focus on scientific claims and evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage and moderate discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion Moderator duties: encourage and moderate active discussions for each submission
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a submission does not receive enough attention, actively engage with assigned reviewers and authors to ask for clarification or argument. Moderate discussion by discouraging participation irrelevant to scientific claims and merits, and prevent toxic behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage reviewers to respond to author rebuttals
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage reviewers to respond to author rebuttals
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt reviewers to engage with author responses so the discussion addresses open concerns and helps reach an informed decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify violations of Code of Ethics during discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify any violations of Code of Ethics during the discussion phase
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If ethical concerns arise in submissions, reviews, or discussion comments, flag the problematic content and contact the Program Chairs; collect relevant evidence to support escalation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act as a scientific expert in discussions
rubrics_metrics.description: Participate in discussions with your own view of the paper
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACs are expected to contribute their expert assessment (not only moderate). Ask authors for clarifications when needed and provide your own perspective to help judge contributions fairly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand and enforce multi-stage discussion rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Multi-Stage Discussion: understand the roles and visibility rules across stages
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stage 1 (Public Discussion): anyone can post comments; authors may post anonymously; assigned reviewers and ACs may post further comments; public commentators cannot post anonymously. Stage 2 (Author/Reviewer/AC Discussion): authors, assigned reviewers and ACs can post; public posts will be blinded until after decisions. Reviewers and ACs may have private discussion threads throughout (remain private after final decision).

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-review content: describe submission and missing elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Meta-review should include a concise description of the submission’s main content (scientific claims and findings), including strengths and weaknesses
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ideally this description should contain both what is discussed in the submission and what is missing from the submission. Base it on your own reading and reviewers' characterization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-review content: summarize discussion and responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Meta-review should contain a concise summary of discussion
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List the points that were raised by the reviewers, how each point was addressed by the authors, and whether the AC found each point worth consideration in decision making. Because ICLR has multiple weeks of discussion, explicitly summarize how discussion affected the assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-review content: give clear recommendation and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Meta-review should end with a clear indication of your recommendation and justification
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The recommendation must be justified based on the submission content and the discussion summary; explain why accept or reject follows from the issues described above.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-review length guideline
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim to write a meta-review of at least 60 words
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a minimum target to ensure meta-reviews are sufficiently informative for authors; longer and more detailed meta-reviews are encouraged when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to the provided AC timeline and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow the AC timeline: bidding, receiving/confirming assignments, vetting reviewer-paper assignments, review period, substitute review period, paper discussion, AC meta-review period, author notification
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key dates provided (e.g., abstract submission Sep 28, paper submission Oct 5, review period Oct 14–Nov 1, paper discussion Nov 9–29, AC meta-review Nov 29–Dec 6, author notification Jan 24). Allow for small last-minute adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure fairness and expertise in assignment and judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Help the Program Chairs manage the reviewing process so every submission is judged fairly and expertly
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend appropriate reviewers, replace delinquent reviewers, and intervene in discussions to ensure balanced and expert assessment across submissions.
